feature: A label can wear a box as well as an outline on its letters
summary: A Border on a label now says what it goes round. Letters draws a line round each letter, the way a caption over a screenshot wants; Box draws a plain rectangle round the label itself, which had no way to be asked for since the Outline row left Appearance. A label can wear one of each at once.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. The Effects list is behind next-shape-parts, which is on by default.

try.do: Open a screenshot, press T, click on it and type a few words.
Press Escape, then press the plus on the Effects header and choose Border.
Read the Border row: it says Follows Letters, and there is no Position row.
Drag its Width up and watch the line grow round each letter.
Try Position Inside and Outside on it, and drag Corner Radius in Appearance to round the box.
Add a second Border from the plus: it arrives on the letters, so the label wears both.
Open a document you bordered a label in before today and check its outline is where you left it.

evaluate: Is Follows the word you would look for, or were you hunting for something called Shape or Around?
Should a new Border on a label still arrive on the letters, or should a label's first border be a box?
The box hugs the words tight, because it follows the label's frame and a label's frame is snug. Does it want room inside it?
With one of each on, does the list read clearly, or do two rows both called Border need telling apart in the header as well?
Position vanishing when the ring follows the letters: helpful, or does a row that changes shape underneath you feel unsteady?
rough: The grip between a letter border and a box border does nothing you can see. A letter outline is baked into the words and a box ring is laid round them afterwards, so the box always paints over, whichever order the list holds. Order among borders of the same kind is real.
There is no padding between the words and the box, because the box follows the label's frame. A roomier bordered label needs room on a text layer, which is its own piece of work.
A gradient poured into a border only shows on a box: an outline round the letters is drawn in the flat colour the gradient stands for. That was true before this change and is unchanged by it.
Screen Recording was granted, so the three pictures are real captures of the probe window, not offscreen renders.
